title: How Europeans can contain Netanyahu’s caretaker government - European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Israel's election produced deadlock (Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot opposition 48, Palestinian citizen parties a record 19), leaving Netanyahu's far-right coalition as a caretaker government with war powers. Oppenheim warns it may renew Iran strikes with Trump after the US midterms or escalate in the West Bank, and urges Europeans to use their own leverage now since any successor will not reverse Israel's illiberal turn.

insights.claim: Preliminary results of Israel's election give no bloc the 61-seat majority: Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's Zionist opposition 48, and Palestinian citizen parties Ra'am and the Joint List a historic 19.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Prolonged Israeli political paralysis raises policy uncertainty for regional risk pricing.

insights.claim: An Eisenkot-led government would require the support of both Palestinian citizen parties, but among the opposition only the Democrats' Yair Golan has argued for such a deal, so all paths likely lead back to Netanyahu via a unity government or fresh 2027 elections.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Base case is Netanyahu retaining power, implying continuity of hawkish policy.

insights.claim: Fresh Israeli elections in 2027 may be more favourable to Netanyahu than the current result.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Extended caretaker period and possible snap vote extend the window of hawkish governance.

insights.claim: Netanyahu's far-right coalition remains in place as a caretaker government that retains the power to wage war, and the new Knesset would have no power to stop a war.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Institutional checks on Israeli military escalation are weak during the caretaker period.
insights.quote: The new Knesset would have no power to stop a war.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Netanyahu's far-right coalition stays on

insights.claim: Netanyahu may renew strikes on Iran together with Donald Trump after the US midterm elections, partly to force the opposition into a unity government in the name of security and rally his base ahead of possible new elections.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Post-midterm window is a flagged tail-risk date for renewed Israel/US-Iran conflict and oil/shipping disruption.
insights.quote: Netanyahu may renew strikes on Iran with Donald Trump after the US midterm elections.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Netanyahu's far-right coalition stays on

insights.claim: If Trump refuses to back strikes on Iran, Netanyahu could instead ramp up his military campaign in the West Bank.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Escalation risk shifts rather than disappears if the Iran option is blocked.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Netanyahu's far-right coalition stays on

insights.claim: Europeans should publicly join Arab partners in opposing a new war with Iran, building on the E4+R4 meeting in Istanbul, and should deny the use of their bases for strikes unless Washington demonstrates an imminent threat.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: European basing denial could constrain the logistics of any renewed US strike campaign.
insights.quote: Unless Washington demonstrates an imminent threat, Europeans should deny the use of their bases for strikes.

insights.claim: European capitals with the best access to Trump should warn him that Israeli escalation against Iran or in the West Bank would threaten gains in Gaza and Lebanon and thwart his vision of Israel's regional integration.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Regional normalisation narrative is a lever that could restrain escalation.

insights.claim: Europeans have offered almost EUR 900m for Gaza's recovery under the UN-endorsed plan and could step up technical support for policing, governance and decommissioning Hamas's weapons.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Signals scale of European reconstruction commitment in Gaza.
insights.quote: Europeans have offered almost €900m for Gaza’s recovery under the UN-endorsed plan

insights.claim: Europe should keep advancing measures against settlement entities, prepare wider measures in case of caretaker-government escalation, and offer a bilateral reset and regional normalisation if the next Israeli government includes Palestinian citizen parties and returns to diplomacy.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Escalating EU sanctions on settlement-linked entities is a live compliance risk for exposed firms.

insights.claim: Israeli Jews are more divided over Netanyahu personally than over his policies, and the opposition has largely embraced his hawkish post-October 7th security doctrine.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: A change of leader would not materially change Israeli security policy; do not price in a dovish pivot.
insights.quote: Israeli Jews are more divided over Netanyahu than over his policies.
insights.locator: Israel's deadlock masks a deeper ideological shift

insights.claim: Citing ECFR's 'The Ideas of Israel', the author argues illiberal and ethno-nationalist ideas have gone mainstream in Israel, so whoever becomes prime minister Europe will face an illiberal Israel whose reliance on force collides with European interests.
insights.speaker: Beth Oppenheim
insights.so_what: Structural EU-Israel friction likely persists across governments, relevant to trade and defence ties.
insights.quote: Whoever emerges as prime minister, Europe faces an illiberal Israel whose reliance on force will collide with European interests.
insights.locator: Israel's deadlock masks a deeper ideological shift
